title: Saving for a Bicycle
story:
Mateo wanted a used bicycle for the ride to school. The price was one hundred and twenty euros, but his jar held only eighteen euros. He wrote a plan at the kitchen table. Each week he would save at least ten euros. He wrote the word goal on a card and taped it above his desk.

Two jobs helped him earn money. On weekday mornings he walked a dog for his neighbour Rosa, who paid four euros a walk. On Saturdays he sold old books at a street stall. Some Saturdays brought six euros, and others brought only two. He dropped every coin into the jar before he spent anything. When friends bought snacks, Mateo drank water and kept his money in his pocket.

Rain made the second month hard. Rosa left town, so the walks stopped for two weeks. Mateo also paid five euros for a bus when his shoes were soaked. He sat down to count the jar and found seventy-four euros. He asked the owner to hold the bicycle for one more month, and the price stayed the same.

Mateo then washed two cars every Sunday for eight euros. He sold old trainers for ten euros too. After three months the jar held one hundred and twenty-five euros. He paid the shop, rode home, and kept five euros for a new bell.

To get money by doing work.
A small outdoor table where things are sold.
To find how many there are.
To keep something for somebody for a time.

quiz.question: What was the price of the bicycle?
quiz.explanation: The shop price was one hundred and twenty euros.
quiz.supportingSentence: The price was one hundred and twenty euros, but his jar held only eighteen euros.

quiz.question: Who paid him for the morning dog walks?
quiz.explanation: Rosa paid four euros each time he walked her dog.
quiz.supportingSentence: On weekday mornings he walked a dog for his neighbour Rosa, who paid four euros a walk.

quiz.question: What work did he add every Sunday?
options: He sold books at a stall
He rode the bus to school
quiz.explanation: Every Sunday he washed two cars and received eight euros.
quiz.supportingSentence: Mateo then washed two cars every Sunday for eight euros.

quiz.question: In this story, what is a stall?
options: A small outdoor table for selling things
A jar used to keep coins
A card taped above a desk
quiz.correctAnswer: A small outdoor table for selling things
quiz.explanation: He sold old books at the stall, so it is a place for selling.
quiz.supportingSentence: On Saturdays he sold old books at a street stall.

quiz.question: Why did Mateo drink water while his friends bought snacks?
options: He was trying not to spend his savings
The shop had no snacks left
Rosa had told him to drink water
He had already bought a new bell
quiz.correctAnswer: He was trying not to spend his savings
quiz.explanation: He kept his money in his pocket instead of buying snacks.
quiz.supportingSentence: When friends bought snacks, Mateo drank water and kept his money in his pocket.
